title: Grade 7 Math — Mon, May 18
description: Probability — Day 1 of 5: What is chance?
subject: mathematics

questions.question: What does probability measure?
options: The exact time an event will happen
How likely an event is to occur
The number of times an event has occurred
questions.explanation: Probability measures how likely (how much chance) an event is to happen, from impossible (0) to certain (1).

questions.question: When you toss a fair coin, how many possible outcomes are there?
questions.explanation: A coin has two faces: Heads (H) and Tails (T). So there are 2 possible outcomes.

questions.question: When you roll a fair six-sided die, how many possible outcomes are there?
questions.explanation: A die has faces numbered 1 to 6. So there are 6 possible outcomes.

questions.question: What is the set of all possible outcomes of an experiment called?
questions.explanation: The sample space is the collection of ALL possible outcomes. For a coin: S = {H, T}. For a die: S = {1,2,3,4,5,6}.

questions.question: If an event is CERTAIN to happen, its probability is:
questions.explanation: A certain event always happens, so P = 1. Example: Sun rising tomorrow.

questions.question: If an event is IMPOSSIBLE, its probability is:
questions.explanation: An impossible event can never happen, so P = 0. Example: Rolling a 7 on a standard die.

questions.question: What is the formula for probability of an event E?
questions.explanation: P(E) = Number of favourable outcomes ÷ Total number of outcomes.

questions.question: What is the probability of getting a Head when tossing a fair coin?
What is the probability of getting 4 when rolling a fair die?
A bag has 3 red and 3 blue balls. What is P(red)?
Probability of any event lies between:
questions.explanation: Probability is always between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain), inclusive.

questions.question: Rolling a die: P(getting an even number)?
questions.explanation: Even numbers on a die: 2, 4, 6 → 3 outcomes. P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.question: Which of these events has a probability of exactly 0?
options: Getting a head on a coin toss
Getting a 7 on a standard 6-sided die
Getting an odd number on a die
Drawing a red card from a deck
questions.explanation: A standard die has faces 1–6 only. Getting 7 is impossible → P = 0.

questions.question: In an experiment, an 'outcome' is:
options: A result of one trial of the experiment
questions.explanation: An outcome is what happens in a single trial of an experiment (e.g., getting H in one coin toss).
